content_html_sanitized:
Last Sunday, the UK publication, The IPaper, carried an outrageous story about the difficulty getting access to medical cannabis in the UK.

See My fight for medicinal cannabis against a 'wild west' of private providers

 

The story begins with a heroic British mother who had to fight the UK government to get cannabis for her son, who has a form of epilepsy that can only be treated with cannabis that has both THC and CBD.

 

Then when she forced the UK government to allow her to give her son the only medicine that works, the battle shifted to the bizarre rules that forces her and many others to pay exorbitant prices for their medicine rather than get through the UK’s National Health Service… because the British government requires more research to prove what everyone already knows.

 

The governments and medical establishments of most of the advanced countries have ignored the science behind the medical uses of cannabis for decades. From MarijuanaNews see My Problem and how I solved it, "I broke the law to save my son." by Cheryl Johnson* Sept. 1997

 

1997!?! How time flies, when you’re not in pain and not in prison.

 

Meanwhile, Charlotte Caldwell, whose campaign after her son Billy's medicine was seized at Heathrow led to a change in the law, said “families are still at the mercy of rogue operators.”

 

Charlotte Caldwell’s determination to get medicinal cannabis for her son Billy’s severe epilepsy led to a change in the law, but thousands of patients are still struggling to get similar treatment

 

Patients are being forced to rely on a “wild west” of private medicinal cannabis providers with a lack of research hampering families in getting the medicine they need, a campaigning mother has said.

 

She isn’t the only mother being forced to battle the Prohibitionists to get medicine for her child.

See

Teagan Appleby's fight for cannabis prescription continues

And

'Hundreds' seek private clinics for medical cannabis

 

Caldwell, whose high-profile media campaign after her son Billy’s medicine was seized at Heathrow airport seven years ago led to a change in the law, said a lack of NHS availability of whole-plant medicinal cannabis is leaving families at the mercy of rogue operators.

As a baby, Billy suffered from a dangerous form of epilepsy that caused prolonged or multiple seizures – as many as 300 a day – but is now “thriving” according to his mother, enjoying activities like horse-riding and swimming, after securing a lifelong supply of whole-plant medicinal cannabis. He is one of less than five people who receive the unlicensed treatment on the NHS as it contains THC, the chemical compound in cannabis that makes you high.

According to the BBC, “Hundreds of people in the UK are turning to private clinics for medical cannabis. Since its legalisation in November 2018, there have been very few, if any, prescriptions for medical cannabis containing THC on the NHS. And this has led some patients, with conditions such as epilepsy and MS, to pay up to £800 a month privately. The government said it sympathised with families "dealing so courageously with challenging conditions". I am sure that makes them feel better.

 

Caldwell says a lack of research is preventing tens of thousands of other patients from accessing similar treatment. “It is seven years since Billy changed the law and there is no research being carried out in the UK in whole-plant medical cannabis.”  Gosh! Only seven years!

 

And who gets medical cannabis on the NHS? Only specialist clinicians can prescribe it.  Why?

 

The NHS has handed out more than 24,000 prescriptions for licensed cannabis-based medicines since it was legalised in November 2018.

 

Billy, now 19, is ‘thriving’ after securing a lifelong NHS prescription of whole-plant medicinal cannabis.

 

“However, growing research has suggested that THC can help people in severe pain. Whole-plant medicinal cannabis, which Billy is prescribed, is legalised for use in the UK but is not widely prescribed on the NHS. As such, the private market has seen a rapid increase in patients with some clinics seeing a ten-fold rise.”

 

The UK government is sacrificing sick and dying patients to satisfy the police and the politicians.

See Following Up On The London Mayor’s Commission Recommendation That Small Amounts of Cannabis Should Be Decriminalized. I Hate It When I’m Right.

 

“Caldwell believes manufacturers are shying away from research into whole-plant medicinal cannabis products, high in THC, due to the fact they are already selling the medicine on the private market. This means treatments such as Billy’s remain unlicensed and therefore virtually impossible to get hold of on the NHS.”

 

Of course, it would be much less expensive if the government would just get out of the way. Cannabis is growing all over the UK, but it is in hidden grow ops for the huge black market. Patients should be able to join cooperatives and grow their own cannabis.

 

“The I Am Billy Foundation that Caldwell now runs is inundated with stories from families who are struggling to access the right medicine or being forced to pay thousands of pounds for a private prescription.

Last year, private cannabis prescriptions doubled – reaching nearly 180,000 – according to the Care Quality Commission (CQC). Experts say this is partly due to a crucial error in the medicinal cannabis legislation as the bill made no distinction on the type of cannabis product which could be used.”

 

“The biggest barrier to patients getting an NHS prescription is the lack of research, trials and studies and the lack of consistent, quality supply of medicinal cannabis.”

 

“NHS England and the National Institute of Health and Care Research has agreed over £8.5m in funding for two world first clinical trials relating to the use of cannabis-based products for medicinal use for the treatment of drug-resistant epilepsies and neuropathic pain due to chemotherapy.”

 

Actually, this is more ritual than research. Science is science on both sides of the Atlantic and even on both sides of the North Sea. They know the answers before they ask the questions. Medical science is supposed to help patients, not delay treatments and cause unnecessary complications in their treatment.

See Dr. Lester Grinspoon Warns About The Pharmaceuticalization of Cannabis, As GW Pharmaceutical Hits All Time High After Deal With Bayer. But Does It Need Prohibition In Order to Succeed?
